newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil expert says hitman killed corruption figure.
newsitem.headline: Brazil expert says hitman killed corruption figure.

text.p: A forensic expert said on Monday the murder of a central figure in one of Brazil's biggest corruption scandals was the work of a professional assassin, not his girlfriend, as stated in an official report.

A report given to a judge in charge of the case showed Paulo Cesar Farias, a close aide of former President Fernando Collor, and his girlfriend, Suzana Marcolino, were the victims of a double homicide, forensic expert George Sanguinetti said.

A police report on the June 1996 killings in the northeastern state of Alagoas concluded Marcolino shot Farias in the chest as he lay in bed in his beachside home before turning the gun on herself. But that version has been repeatedly contested by Sanguinetti, a leading police forensic expert, who earlier this year was asked to draw up his own report into the killings.

"There was no sign of a crime of passion in that bedroom," Sanguinetti told national CBN radio, adding that Farias was shot to death elsewhere by someone taller than himself with a precise, "professional" shot. He also said Marcolino's body showed signs of a struggle before she was shot.
"Suzana was used as part of a setup that this was a crime of passion," Sanguinetti told CBN. "There are a lot of people who are interested in (Faria's) death."

Farias was killed shortly before he was due to testify in court about an influence-peddling racket he was alleged to have masterminded. The scandal brought down Collor in December 1992 but the former president since has been cleared of any wrongdoing.
